capsian.name: Capsian
capsian.summary: An Epipalaeolithic culture of Algeria and Tunisia from about 9000 to 5400 BCE, named after the town of Gafsa, known for a varied hunting diet and early decorative art.

aurochs.name: Aurochs
aurochs.summary: An extinct wild ancestor of domestic cattle, once found from western Europe to East Asia, with the last known individual dying in the late 17th or early 18th century.

tassili-n-ajjer.name: Tassili n'Ajjer
tassili-n-ajjer.summary: A Sahara Desert mountain range in southeastern Algeria holding one of the world's most important groupings of prehistoric cave art, designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

african-humid-period.name: African humid period
african-humid-period.summary: A wetter climate phase in Africa during the late Pleistocene and Holocene, when the Sahara was covered in grasses, trees and lakes, lasting roughly from 14,600 to about 5,000 years ago.

epipalaeolithic.name: Epipalaeolithic
epipalaeolithic.summary: An archaeological period between the Upper Paleolithic and Neolithic, roughly 20,000 to 10,000 BP in the Levant, marked by nomadic hunter-gatherers making small stone tools called microliths.

tamanrasset.name: Tamanrasset
tamanrasset.summary: An oasis city in southern Algeria's Ahaggar Mountains, chief city of the Algerian Tuareg, originally established as a military outpost on trans-Saharan trade routes.

medjez-amar.name: Medjez Amar
medjez-amar.summary: A small town in Guelma Province, Algeria, with a population of about 6,426 as of the 1998 census.

constantine-algeria.name: Constantine
constantine-algeria.summary: Capital of Constantine Province in northeastern Algeria, known as Cirta in Roman times before being renamed after Emperor Constantine the Great; nicknamed the 'City of Bridges'.

numidia.name: Numidia
numidia.summary: An ancient Berber kingdom in what is now Algeria and parts of Tunisia and Libya, unified by King Masinissa during the Second Punic War and later a Roman client state.

berber-languages.name: Berber languages
berber-languages.summary: A branch of the Afroasiatic language family, also called Tamazight or Amazigh, spoken by indigenous Berber communities across North Africa, mainly in Morocco and Algeria.

strait-of-sicily.name: Strait of Sicily
strait-of-sicily.summary: Strait between Sicily and Tunisia dividing the western and eastern Mediterranean Sea, historically known as a crossroads of the Mediterranean.

bab-al-mandab-strait.name: Bab al-Mandab Strait
bab-al-mandab-strait.summary: A strategic strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and Indian Ocean.

gafsa.name: Gafsa
gafsa.summary: City in Tunisia, capital of Gafsa Governorate, known in Latin as Capsa.

acacus-mountains.name: Tadrart Acacus
acacus-mountains.summary: A mountain range in the Sahara desert of western Libya, noted for its rich collection of prehistoric rock art.

chellala-district.name: Chellala District
chellala-district.summary: A district in Algeria's El Abiodh Sidi Cheikh Province, named after its capital town, Chellala.

meknes.name: Meknes
meknes.summary: One of Morocco's four imperial cities, founded in the 11th century by the Almoravids and made capital by Sultan Ismail Ibn Sharif (1672–1727).
